existing.eligibility_summary: Overseas fee-paying students from lower-income backgrounds. Up to 85 scholarships for 2026/27 (5 ring-fenced for India, 1 for Japan).

existing.funding_period: per year for the normal course duration
eligibility: From any country outside the UK; applications are not accepted from those already residing in the UK
At serious risk as a direct result of armed conflict, and/or displaced from their home country within the last three years because of armed conflict
Has sought international protection outside of the UK
Eligible to pay the Overseas fee rate
Comes from a lower income background
Does not already hold, or is not in the process of gaining, a qualification at or above the level of the course applied for
Holds an offer of a place on a chosen full-time Master's at UCL by the scholarship panel meeting at the start of June 2026
Has a valid passport or other eligible travel document in place by the selection panel meeting so a UK student visa can be applied for
existing.eligibility_summary: Candidates must be from outside the UK, not already resident in the UK, at serious risk or displaced because of armed conflict within the last three years, have sought international protection outside the UK, be eligible for the Overseas fee rate, come from a lower income background, and hold a UCL offer by the scholarship panel meeting in early June.
benefits: Immigration Health Surcharge and visa fee allowance
coverage: Full tuition fees for the normal course duration
Maintenance payment of approximately GBP 20,000 to cover accommodation and living costs
Guaranteed single room in UCL accommodation (the accommodation fee is deducted from the maintenance payment)
Allowance covering the Immigration Health Surcharge and visa fees
documents: Valid passport or other eligible travel document
Evidence of financial need (requested from shortlisted candidates)
Uploaded Word document or PDF answering the three Humanitarian Scholarship questions in the International Master's Awards form
application_method: Submit a complete UCL admission application, including submitted references, before the scholarship deadline
Complete the International Master's Awards form and answer the mandatory Humanitarian Scholarship questions
Upload a Word document or PDF answering the three Humanitarian Scholarship questions
If shortlisted, provide evidence of financial need and of a valid travel document
existing.selection_notes: Awarded on the basis of financial need, on the recommendation of the UCL Humanitarian Scholarship panel. Shortlisted candidates are contacted in mid May; successful candidates are typically informed by late June.
existing.duration: Tenable for one year, unless the full-time programme is two years in length
existing.application_period: The 2026/27 cycle closed at 5pm BST on Thursday 7 May 2026. UCL has not yet published the date for the following annual cycle.
existing.program_type: Humanitarian scholarship for conflict-displaced postgraduate students
